speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked	the Minister for Transport whether the Ministry will review and control the number of vehicles that can be used for private vehicle hire in addition to the vocational licence requirement for such car drivers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is a public concern that if you do not control the number of such vehicles, it will actually affect the current system because, currently, taxi companies are exempted from Certificate of Entitlement (COE) bidding.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, whether it will lead to higher COE prices for private vehicles.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I am quite certain that within the next 10 to 15 years, how we move from Point A to Point B will be quite different from what we are doing today, and from what we are more familiar with, partly because of technology,  disruptive business models and rising expectations from commuters.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, what will be the likely steady state scenario of our transport scene?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is not something that the Government can determine in a top-down approach.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The best approach, I think, is to let Singaporeans, consumers and commuters, decide.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For example, in this whole new space of private hire, point-to-point transport, exemplified by Grab and Uber, the whole scenario is still changing.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: At the same time, what is comforting is that the number of taxi trips chalked up by taxi drivers has remained quite stable.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That means that the new players have been meeting new demands or under- or unmet demands in the past.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As I said, we cannot tell how it would be like in 10 or 15 years' time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is best that we leave it to the market, meaning leave it to Singaporeans and consumers, to decide.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Our operating principle must be: does it improve services to the commuters?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Does it lift the quality of life of Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If it does, then, as a regulator, we should try to nudge it in that direction.
